Q1 What is JavaScript?High frequency
ANSWER
JavaScript is a programming language used to add logic and interaction to web pages. It can also run on servers through Node.js.
EXAMPLE
The same language can handle a browser button click and implement a Node.js API route, although each runtime provides different host APIs.

Q2 What does dynamically typed mean?
ANSWER
Dynamically typed means a variable can hold values of different types while the program is running. We do not fix the variable's type when declaring it.
EXAMPLE
The code let x = 10; x = "hello"; is valid because the binding is not permanently restricted to one type.

Q3 What is the difference between var, let, and const?High frequency
ANSWER
var is function-scoped and can be redeclared. let is block-scoped and can be reassigned. const is block-scoped and cannot be reassigned.
COMPARISON
Feature                  | var                 | let                  | const
Scope                    | Function            | Block                | Block
Reassignment             | Allowed             | Allowed              | Not allowed
Same-scope redeclaration | Allowed             | Not allowed          | Not allowed
Before declaration       | undefined           | ReferenceError       | ReferenceError
Initializer required     | No                  | No                   | Yes
EXAMPLE 1 - SCOPE
function checkScope() {
  if (true) {
    var functionScoped = 1;
    let blockScoped = 2;
    const alsoBlockScoped = 3;
  }

  console.log(functionScoped);
  console.log(blockScoped);
}
OUTPUT
1
ReferenceError: blockScoped is not defined
EXAMPLE 2 - REASSIGNMENT
var first = 1;
first = 2;                 // Valid

let second = 1;
second = 2;                // Valid

const third = 1;
third = 2;                 // TypeError
RESULT
first stores 2
second stores 2
TypeError: Assignment to constant variable
EXAMPLE 3 - REDECLARATION
Run each case below as a separate script because either SyntaxError prevents that entire script from executing.

var score = 10;
var score = 20;            // Valid
RESULT
score stores 20

let total = 10;
let total = 20;            // SyntaxError in the same scope

const limit = 10;
const limit = 20;          // SyntaxError in the same scope
RESULT FOR EACH SEPARATE CASE
SyntaxError: Identifier has already been declared
EXAMPLE 4 - HOISTING
console.log(oldValue);     // undefined
var oldValue = 10;

console.log(newValue);     // ReferenceError: temporal dead zone
let newValue = 10;
OUTPUT
undefined
ReferenceError: Cannot access 'newValue' before initialization
EXAMPLE 5 - CONST OBJECT
const user = { name: "Harsh" };
user.name = "Amit";        // Valid: object content can change
user = { name: "Amit" };   // TypeError: binding cannot change
RESULT
user.name stores "Amit"
TypeError: Assignment to constant variable
QUICK RULE
Use const by default, use let when reassignment is required, and avoid var in modern JavaScript unless function scope is intentional.

Q4 What is hoisting?High frequency
ANSWER
Hoisting means JavaScript prepares declarations before executing a scope. Function declarations can be called early, var is initially undefined, and let or const cannot be used before initialization.
EXAMPLE
console.log(a); var a = 5; prints undefined, but console.log(b); let b = 5; throws ReferenceError.

Q5 What is temporal dead zone?
ANSWER
The temporal dead zone is the time between entering a block and declaring a let or const variable. Accessing the variable during this time throws a ReferenceError.
EXAMPLE
Inside a block, accessing let count before let count = 1 reaches the temporal dead zone and throws ReferenceError.

EXAMPLE

Q25 What is the difference between call, apply, and bind?High frequency
ANSWER
call runs a function immediately with separate arguments. apply also runs it immediately but accepts an argument array. bind returns a new function to call later.
COMPARISON
Method | Runs immediately | Arguments
call | Yes | Listed separately
apply | Yes | Supplied as an array
bind | No | Returns a reusable function
EXAMPLE
function greet(greeting, punctuation) {
  return greeting + " " + this.name + punctuation;
}

const user = { name: "Harsh" };
greet.call(user, "Hi", "!");          // "Hi Harsh!"
greet.apply(user, ["Hello", "."]);    // "Hello Harsh."
const boundGreet = greet.bind(user, "Hey");
boundGreet("!");                       // "Hey Harsh!"

Q46 What is the event loop?High frequency
ANSWER
The event loop checks whether the call stack is empty and then runs ready callbacks. Promise microtasks are handled before the next timer or I/O task.
EXAMPLE
A timer expires outside JavaScript execution, its callback becomes eligible, and the event loop runs it only after current synchronous code and required microtasks finish.

Q47 What is the call stack?High frequency
ANSWER
The call stack keeps track of currently running function calls. The newest function call finishes first.
EXAMPLE
main() calls foo(), foo() calls bar(); stack is main -> foo -> bar until bar returns.

Q48 What happens if the call stack is blocked?High frequency
ANSWER
If synchronous code blocks the call stack, JavaScript cannot run timers, promise callbacks, user events, or other request handlers until that code finishes.
EXAMPLE
Main thread runs a five-second while loop -> clicks and ready timer callbacks cannot execute during those five seconds.

Q49 What is callback queue?
ANSWER
A callback queue holds callbacks that are ready to run. In practice, browsers and Node.js use different queues for timers, I/O, and microtasks.
EXAMPLE
A ready timer waits in a timer-related task queue, while a fulfilled promise reaction waits in the microtask queue and is processed earlier at the microtask checkpoint.

Q50 What are microtasks?High frequency
ANSWER
Microtasks are small callbacks, mainly promise callbacks, that run after current synchronous code and before the next normal task.
EXAMPLE
Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log("microtask")) runs after current synchronous logs but before an already-ready setTimeout callback.

Q51 What are macrotasks?High frequency
ANSWER
Macrotask is a common name for normal event-loop tasks such as timers, I/O callbacks, and browser events. They run after current microtasks.
EXAMPLE
console.log("A"); setTimeout(()=>console.log("B"),0); console.log("C") -> output is A, C, B because the timer callback is a later task.

Q52 Which runs first: Promise.then or setTimeout 0?High frequency
ANSWER
Promise.then runs before setTimeout(..., 0) in the same turn because promise callbacks are microtasks and timer callbacks run in a later task.
EXAMPLE
Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log(1)); setTimeout(() => console.log(2), 0); prints 1 then 2 after the current synchronous code completes.

Q53 What is async/await internally based on?High frequency
ANSWER
async and await are built on promises. await pauses only that async function and continues it later when the promise settles.
EXAMPLE
const value = await fetchData(); allows other callbacks to run while fetchData is pending, then resumes the function with the fulfillment value or throws the rejection.

Q54 Does async/await create a new thread?High frequency
ANSWER
No. async/await does not create a thread. It pauses an async function and resumes it later through the promise and event-loop system.
EXAMPLE

ANSWER

EXAMPLE
Node can start a DB query, handle another request while waiting, then resume when the DB response returns.

ANSWER
Web APIs are features supplied by the browser, such as the DOM, fetch, timers, storage, and events. They are not part of the JavaScript language itself.

Q57 What is a Promise and what states can it have?High frequency
ANSWER
A Promise represents the future result of an asynchronous operation. It starts pending and becomes either fulfilled with a value or rejected with an error.
EXAMPLE
fetch("/api/user") returns a pending Promise. A successful response fulfills it; a network failure rejects it.

Q58 What is Promise chaining?High frequency
ANSWER
Promise chaining passes each result to the next then callback and sends errors to the nearest catch. Returning a Promise makes the next step wait for it.
EXAMPLE
fetch(url).then(r => r.json()).then(saveUser).catch(handleError) runs the steps in order without nested callbacks.

Q59 What is the difference between Promise.all and Promise.allSettled?High frequency
ANSWER
Promise.all fulfills when every Promise fulfills and rejects immediately when one rejects. Promise.allSettled waits for every Promise and returns each outcome.
EXAMPLE
Use Promise.all when three required API calls must all succeed. Use allSettled when showing every upload result even if one upload fails.

Q60 What is the difference between Promise.race and Promise.any?
ANSWER
Promise.race settles with the first settled Promise, whether success or failure. Promise.any fulfills with the first successful Promise and rejects only if all reject.
EXAMPLE
Race a request against a timeout with Promise.race. Query backup endpoints with Promise.any when any successful response is acceptable.

Q61 What does an async function return?High frequency
ANSWER
An async function always returns a Promise. A returned normal value becomes a fulfilled Promise, and a thrown error becomes a rejected Promise.
EXAMPLE
async function getCount(){ return 3; } returns a Promise that fulfills with 3.

Q62 What exactly does await do?High frequency
ANSWER
await pauses only the current async function until its Promise settles. The JavaScript thread remains free to run other work, and the function continues through a microtask.
EXAMPLE
While await fetch(url) is waiting, Node or the browser can handle timers, events, and other requests; code after await resumes later.

Q63 How do you handle errors with async/await?High frequency
ANSWER
Use try/catch around awaited operations, or let the async function reject and handle that rejection at its caller.
EXAMPLE
try { const user = await loadUser(); } catch (error) { log(error); } handles a rejected loadUser Promise.
Previous Next
Q64 What is callback hell and how do you avoid it?High frequency
ANSWER
Callback hell is deeply nested asynchronous callbacks that make control flow and error handling difficult. Promises, async/await, and small named functions flatten the flow.
EXAMPLE
Replace readFile(... db.save(... sendEmail(...))) nesting with await readFile(); await db.save(); await sendEmail().
Previous Next
Q65 What is the difference between concurrency and parallelism?High frequency
ANSWER
Concurrency means tasks overlap in progress. Parallelism means tasks execute at the same instant on different CPU cores or workers.
EXAMPLE
One event loop can concurrently manage many waiting network requests. Two worker threads can run two CPU calculations in parallel.

Q117 What is React?High frequency

Q124 What is reconciliation?High frequency

Q164 What is Node.js thread pool?High frequency
ANSWER
Node.js uses a libuv thread pool for selected work such as file operations, encryption, compression, and some DNS tasks. This keeps that work away from the main JavaScript thread.
EXAMPLE
crypto.pbkdf2 starts -> a libuv worker performs the expensive operation while the main JavaScript thread can handle other events.

Q165 What is blocking code?High frequency
ANSWER
Blocking code keeps the main JavaScript thread busy and prevents other callbacks or requests from running until it finishes.
EXAMPLE
JSON.parse spends two seconds on the main thread -> all other JavaScript callbacks wait for those two seconds.

Q166 What is non-blocking I/O?High frequency
ANSWER
Non-blocking I/O starts an operation and lets JavaScript continue other work while waiting. Its result is handled later through a callback or promise.
EXAMPLE
Starting a DB query and using await is non-blocking for other incoming requests.
Previous Next
Q167 Why is Node good for I/O-heavy APIs?High frequency
ANSWER
Node.js is good for I/O-heavy APIs because it can handle many requests while they wait for databases, files, or network responses without blocking one thread per request.
EXAMPLE
A REST API waiting on MongoDB can serve other users while the DB operation is pending.

Q168 Why is Node not ideal for CPU-heavy synchronous work?High frequency
ANSWER
CPU-heavy synchronous work keeps Node's main thread busy. During that time, other requests and callbacks must wait.
EXAMPLE
Image processing or huge loops in the main thread can delay all API responses.
Previous Next
Q169 How to handle CPU-heavy work in Node?High frequency
ANSWER
I move CPU-heavy work to worker threads, child processes, background workers, or a separate service so the main event loop stays responsive.
EXAMPLE
Move CPU-heavy PDF processing to a worker thread, queue worker, or separate process.
Previous Next
Q170 What is concurrency in Node?High frequency
ANSWER
Concurrency means several tasks make progress during overlapping time. On one Node.js event loop, their JavaScript callbacks still run one at a time.
EXAMPLE
Request A waits on MongoDB while Node starts B through Z -> their lifetimes overlap even though JavaScript callbacks run one at a time.
Previous Next
Q171 What are the main Node.js event loop phases?
ANSWER
Node moves through phases for timers, pending callbacks, polling I/O, check callbacks, and close callbacks. Microtasks run between callback executions.
EXAMPLE
setTimeout runs in the timers phase, many I/O callbacks run around poll, and setImmediate runs in the check phase.

Q172 What is process.nextTick compared with a Promise microtask?
ANSWER
Node runs the process.nextTick queue before the regular Promise microtask queue after the current operation. Overusing nextTick can delay I/O.
EXAMPLE
process.nextTick(logA); Promise.resolve().then(logB); generally logs A before B in Node.

Q173 What is setImmediate compared with setTimeout(fn, 0)?
ANSWER
setImmediate runs in Node's check phase, while setTimeout runs after its minimum timer delay in the timers phase. Their order depends on where they were scheduled.
EXAMPLE
Inside an I/O callback, setImmediate commonly runs before setTimeout(fn, 0); from top-level code the order is not guaranteed.

Q174 What are worker threads in Node.js?High frequency
ANSWER
Worker threads run JavaScript in separate threads with separate event loops, making them useful for CPU-heavy JavaScript. They communicate through messages or shared memory.
EXAMPLE
The API thread sends a large calculation to a Worker; the worker computes it on another core and posts the result back.

Q175 What is the difference between worker threads, child processes, and cluster?
ANSWER
Worker threads are threads inside one process. Child processes are separate OS processes. Cluster creates multiple Node processes that can share incoming server traffic.
EXAMPLE
Use a worker thread for CPU calculation, spawn a child process for an isolated command, and use cluster to run an HTTP server across CPU cores.

Q176 What is Node.js?High frequency

EXAMPLE

Node.js is useful for backend APIs because its non-blocking I/O can handle many requests that spend time waiting for databases or networks.
EXAMPLE

Q187 What is Express.js?High frequency

req.params contains values taken from named parts of the route path, such as id from /users/:id.

Q193 What is req.body?

Q194 What is next()?

Q195 What is error-handling middleware?High frequency

Express error middleware has four parameters: error, request, response, and next. It converts errors into a consistent HTTP response.

REST APIS AND JWT

33 questions

Q198 What is REST API?High frequency
ANSWER
A REST API treats data as resources identified by URLs and uses standard HTTP methods and status codes. Each request should contain the information needed to process it.
EXAMPLE
GET /users/1 reads a user, POST /users creates one, and PATCH /users/1 changes selected fields; each protected request also carries authentication.
Previous Next
Q199 GET vs POST?High frequency
ANSWER
GET reads data and should not change server state. POST usually creates a resource or starts an action and is not automatically idempotent.
COMPARISON
Aspect | GET | POST
Purpose | Read resource data | Submit data for processing
Safe | Yes | No by default
Idempotent | Yes | No by default
Cacheable | Defined as cacheable | Only with explicit freshness rules
EXAMPLE
GET /products lists products without changing server state; POST /products creates a product, while POST /search could perform a complex read without creating one.
Previous Next
Q200 PUT vs PATCH?High frequency
ANSWER
PUT usually replaces the complete resource at a URL. PATCH changes only selected fields.
COMPARISON
Aspect | PUT | PATCH
Meaning | Replace the full resource | Change selected fields
Missing fields | May be removed/reset | Usually unchanged
Idempotency | Defined idempotent | Depends on patch operation
EXAMPLE
PUT /profiles/42 with the complete profile replaces profile 42, while PATCH /profiles/42 with { "name": "Harsh" } changes only the name under this API contract.
Previous Next
Q201 DELETE idempotent?High frequency
ANSWER
DELETE should be idempotent: repeating it should leave the resource deleted. Later calls may return a different status, but they should not create another state change.
EXAMPLE
The first DELETE /users/1 may return 204 and the second 404, but after either sequence the user remains absent and no second deletion side effect occurs.
Previous Next
Q202 What do common HTTP status codes mean?High frequency
ANSWER
2xx means success, 4xx means a client-side problem, and 5xx means a server-side problem. Common codes include 200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429, and 500.
COMPARISON
Code | Meaning | Typical use
200 | OK | Successful read or update with a response body
201 | Created | A resource was created
202 | Accepted | Work was accepted for asynchronous processing
204 | No Content | Success with no response body
400 | Bad Request | Malformed or invalid request
401 | Unauthorized | Authentication is missing or invalid
403 | Forbidden | Authenticated but not allowed
404 | Not Found | Resource does not exist
409 | Conflict | Request conflicts with current state
422 | Unprocessable Content | Well-formed request fails semantic validation
429 | Too Many Requests | Rate limit exceeded
500 | Internal Server Error | Unexpected server failure
EXAMPLE
Creating a user can return 201, accepting a report export for background processing can return 202, a missing token returns 401, and an authenticated user without an admin role receives 403.
Previous Next
Q203 Authentication vs authorization?High frequency
ANSWER
Authentication checks who the user is. Authorization checks what that authenticated user is allowed to do.
COMPARISON
Aspect | Authentication | Authorization
Question | Who are you? | What may you do?
Example | Verify password/token | Check role or ownership
Order | Usually first | After identity is known
EXAMPLE
A valid token authenticates user 42; an ownership or role check then authorizes whether user 42 may delete document 99.
Previous Next
Q204 What is JWT?High frequency
ANSWER
JWT is a signed token format used to carry claims between systems. The signature lets the server detect whether the token was changed.
EXAMPLE
An access token can contain sub, role, iss, aud, and exp; the API verifies its signature and claims before trusting the user identity.
Previous Next
Q205 JWT structure?High frequency
ANSWER
A JWT has three base64url-encoded parts: header, payload, and signature. The payload is readable, so secrets must not be stored there.
EXAMPLE
header.payload.signature may encode {"alg":"HS256"}, {"sub":"user-1","exp":1735689600}, and an HMAC over the first two encoded segments.
Previous Next
Q206 What are JWT claims?High frequency
ANSWER
JWT claims are values inside the payload, such as user ID, issuer, audience, expiry time, and roles.
EXAMPLE
{sub:"user-7",exp:future,iss:"auth-api",aud:"docs-api"} -> identifies the subject and limits when, by whom, and for which API the token is valid.
Previous Next
Q207 What is JWT signature?High frequency
ANSWER
The JWT signature is created from the header and payload using a secret or private key. Verification proves that those parts were not changed after signing.
EXAMPLE
Changing role from user to admin invalidates the signature; anyone can still Base64URL-decode an ordinary signed payload, so sensitive data does not belong there.
Previous Next
Q208 Session auth vs JWT auth?High frequency
ANSWER
Session authentication stores user session data on the server and gives the browser a session ID cookie. JWT authentication usually verifies a signed token on each request without a server-side session lookup.
COMPARISON
Aspect | Session authentication | JWT authentication
State | Server-side session record | Claims carried in token
Revocation | Direct session deletion | Requires expiry or revocation design
Scaling | Shared session store often needed | Verification can be stateless
Credential | Random session ID | Signed token
EXAMPLE
Delete session id abc on logout -> its cookie no longer authenticates; a self-contained JWT remains valid until expiry unless revocation state is checked.
Previous Next
Q209 Hashing vs encryption?High frequency
ANSWER
Hashing is one-way and is used for password checking or integrity. Encryption is reversible with a key and is used when the original data must be recovered.
COMPARISON
Aspect | Hashing | Encryption
Direction | One-way | Reversible with key
Password storage | Appropriate slow password hash | Not appropriate alone
Use | Verification/integrity | Confidential data recovery
EXAMPLE
Login verifies a password against its hash without recovering plaintext; encrypted API data must be decrypted with the key to restore the original.
Previous Next
Q210 What is bcrypt?High frequency
ANSWER
bcrypt is a password-hashing algorithm that includes a salt and an adjustable cost, making password guesses deliberately slow.
EXAMPLE
Increasing bcrypt cost from 10 to 12 raises verification work, so choose a cost that is expensive for attackers but still acceptable for login latency and server capacity.

Q211 What is CORS?High frequency
ANSWER
CORS is a browser security rule that lets a server state which other origins may read its responses.
EXAMPLE
An API can return Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com so that browser frontend may read the response, while rejecting or omitting that header for an unapproved origin.

Q212 What is CSRF?High frequency
ANSWER
CSRF is an attack where another site makes a logged-in browser send an unwanted request using credentials the browser adds automatically.
EXAMPLE
A user is logged in to a bank. A malicious site submits a transfer form to that bank, and the browser automatically includes the bank cookie. That is a CSRF attempt.

Q213 How reduce CSRF?
ANSWER
CSRF risk is reduced with SameSite cookies, CSRF tokens, origin checks, and by avoiding state-changing GET requests.
EXAMPLE
Attacker submits a cross-site transfer form -> SameSite cookies and a validated CSRF token prevent an authenticated state-changing request.

Q214 What is XSS?High frequency
ANSWER
XSS happens when untrusted content is executed as JavaScript in another user's browser.
EXAMPLE
Comment contains <img src=x onerror=steal()> and the app injects it as raw HTML -> attacker JavaScript executes in the user's origin.

Q215 How reduce XSS?
ANSWER
I reduce XSS by escaping output, avoiding unsafe HTML insertion, sanitizing allowed HTML, using a Content Security Policy, and keeping sensitive cookies HttpOnly.
EXAMPLE
Render a comment as React text so <script> is escaped; if rich HTML is required, sanitize it with a maintained allowlist before using dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

Q216 What is SQL injection?High frequency
ANSWER
SQL injection happens when untrusted input is joined into an SQL command and changes the command's meaning.
EXAMPLE
Unsafe code joins user input directly into SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '...'. An attacker can add SQL syntax and change the query instead of providing only an email value.

Q217 How prevent SQL injection?
ANSWER
I prevent SQL injection with parameterized queries and least-privilege database accounts. Dynamic table or column names must come from an allowlist.
EXAMPLE
db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = $1", [email]) treats attacker input as one value; a dynamic ORDER BY column must come from an allowlist rather than interpolation.

Q218 What is rate limiting?High frequency
ANSWER
Rate limiting restricts how many requests a client or key can make during a time window. Extra requests are usually rejected with status 429.
EXAMPLE
Sixth login attempt within one minute -> rate limiter returns 429 instead of checking another password.
Previous Next
Q219 What is idempotency?High frequency
ANSWER
Idempotency means repeating the same intended request has the same final server-state effect as processing it once.
EXAMPLE
Two retries carrying the same payment idempotency key return the existing payment result instead of creating a second charge, even if the first response was lost.

Q220 What is request validation?High frequency
ANSWER
Request validation checks incoming data for required fields, types, formats, ranges, and business rules before using it.
EXAMPLE
Signup body has email="bad" and a 3-character password -> validation returns field errors before hashing or database writes begin.

Q221 Why validate on backend?
ANSWER
Backend validation is required because users can bypass frontend checks and call the API directly. Frontend validation only improves user feedback.
EXAMPLE
Browser requires password length 8, but curl sends length 3 directly -> backend validation still rejects it.

Q222 What is stateless API?High frequency
ANSWER
A stateless API does not depend on user data stored only inside one server process. Each request carries the information needed to handle it.
EXAMPLE
Request A and Request B each include a verifiable access token -> either server instance can authenticate them without remembering the previous request.

Q223 What are the main REST constraints?High frequency
ANSWER
REST emphasizes client-server separation, stateless requests, cacheable responses, a uniform resource interface, layered systems, and optional code on demand.
EXAMPLE
GET /users/42 identifies a resource, includes all required auth in the request, and can return cache headers.

Q224 How should an API be versioned?High frequency
ANSWER
Version an API when introducing incompatible contract changes. Common approaches use a URL such as /v1, a request header, or media-type negotiation.
EXAMPLE

Q225 What is content negotiation?High frequency
ANSWER
Content negotiation lets the client and server agree on response and request representations using headers such as Accept and Content-Type.
EXAMPLE
Content-Type: application/json says the request body is JSON; Accept: application/json asks for a JSON response.

Q226 Access token vs refresh token?High frequency
ANSWER
An access token is short-lived and sent to APIs. A refresh token lasts longer and is used only to obtain new access tokens, so it needs stronger storage and rotation controls.

Q227 Why validate JWT issuer and audience?High frequency
ANSWER
Issuer confirms which trusted authority created the token. Audience confirms the token was intended for this API, preventing acceptance of a valid token made for another service.

Q228 Which cookie flags improve authentication security?High frequency
ANSWER
HttpOnly blocks JavaScript access, Secure sends the cookie only over HTTPS, and SameSite limits cross-site sending. Path, Domain, and expiry should also be narrowly configured.

Q229 What is OAuth 2.0?

OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework that lets an application obtain limited access to a resource on a user's behalf without receiving the user's password.

Q230 What is a reverse proxy?

SQL

23 questions

Q233 What is SQL?
ANSWER
SQL is the language used to create, read, update, and manage data in relational databases.
EXAMPLE
users contains (1, 'Harsh') -> SELECT id, name FROM users; returns (1, 'Harsh').
Previous Next
Q234 What are DDL, DML, DCL, and TCL?
ANSWER
DDL changes database structure, DML reads or changes data, DCL controls permissions, and TCL controls transactions.
COMPARISON
Category | Purpose | Common commands
DDL | Define structures | CREATE, ALTER, DROP
DML | Read or change rows | SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
DCL | Manage access | GRANT, REVOKE
TCL | Manage transactions | COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT
EXAMPLE
CREATE TABLE defines a table, INSERT adds a row, GRANT permits access, and ROLLBACK cancels uncommitted transaction changes.
Previous Next
Q235 What is GROUP BY?High frequency
ANSWER
GROUP BY puts rows with the same selected values into groups so aggregate functions can return one result for each group.
EXAMPLE
departments [IT, IT, HR] -> GROUP BY department_id with COUNT(*) returns IT=2 and HR=1.
Previous Next
Q236 What is HAVING?High frequency
ANSWER
WHERE filters rows before grouping. HAVING filters the grouped results and can use aggregate conditions.
EXAMPLE
IT has 8 employees and HR has 3 -> HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 returns only IT after grouping.
Previous Next
Q237 What are the main SQL joins?High frequency
ANSWER
INNER JOIN returns matching rows. LEFT or RIGHT JOIN also keeps unmatched rows from one side. FULL JOIN keeps unmatched rows from both sides, and CROSS JOIN returns every pair.
COMPARISON
Join | Result
INNER | Only rows matching the join condition
LEFT | All left rows plus matching right rows
RIGHT | All right rows plus matching left rows
FULL OUTER | Matches plus unmatched rows from both sides
CROSS | Cartesian product of both inputs
EXAMPLE
Users contains A and B, while only A has an order. INNER JOIN returns A; LEFT JOIN returns A with its order and B with NULL order fields.
Previous Next
Q238 What is UNION?
ANSWER
UNION combines results from compatible queries and removes duplicate rows.
EXAMPLE
customers=[a,b], leads=[b,c] -> UNION returns [a,b,c], removing duplicate b.
Previous Next
Q239 What is UNION ALL?
ANSWER
UNION ALL combines compatible query results without removing duplicates, so it is usually faster than UNION.
EXAMPLE
customers=[a,b], leads=[b,c] -> UNION ALL returns [a,b,b,c], preserving duplicate b.
Previous Next
Q240 What is subquery?High frequency
ANSWER
A subquery is a query written inside another SQL statement. Its result is used by the outer statement.
EXAMPLE
salaries [40,60,80] -> SELECT salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees); returns only 80.
Previous Next
Q241 What is view?
ANSWER
A view is a saved SQL query that can be used like a virtual table. A normal view stores the query, not a separate copy of its result.
EXAMPLE
CREATE VIEW active_users AS SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = TRUE; -> SELECT * FROM active_users reads only active users through the saved query.
Previous Next
Q242 What are aggregate functions?
ANSWER
Aggregate functions turn many rows into a summary value. Common examples are COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX.
EXAMPLE
salaries [40, 60, NULL] -> AVG(salary)=50, COUNT(salary)=2, and COUNT(*)=3.
Previous Next
Q243 What is index in SQL?High frequency
ANSWER
An SQL index is an extra data structure, usually a B-tree, that helps the database find or sort rows without scanning the whole table.
EXAMPLE
Email lookup scans 1,000,000 rows -> CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email); can enable an indexed lookup for that query shape.
Previous Next
Q244 What is query plan?High frequency
ANSWER
A query plan shows how the database plans to run a query, including scans, indexes, joins, sorting, and aggregation.
EXAMPLE
EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM users WHERE email='a@x.com'; -> Index Scan is targeted; Seq Scan means every row may be checked.
Previous Next
Q245 CHAR vs VARCHAR?
ANSWER
CHAR stores fixed-length text and may pad shorter values. VARCHAR stores variable-length text up to a limit.
COMPARISON
Aspect | CHAR(n) | VARCHAR(n)
Length model | Fixed-width semantics | Variable length
Good fit | Consistently sized codes | Names and general text
Padding | Commonly space padded | No fixed padding
EXAMPLE
country_code='IN' -> CHAR(2); name='Harsh Parihar' with varying length -> VARCHAR(255).
Previous Next
Q246 What is pagination?High frequency
ANSWER
Pagination returns a limited, ordered part of a large result. Offset pagination uses page positions, while cursor pagination continues after a known record.
EXAMPLE
With users ordered by id, LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40 returns positions 41-60. Cursor pagination can instead request the next 20 rows with id greater than the last returned id.

Q247 What is the difference between DELETE, TRUNCATE, and DROP?High frequency
ANSWER
DELETE removes selected rows and can use WHERE. TRUNCATE quickly removes all rows while keeping the table. DROP removes the table definition and its data.
EXAMPLE
DELETE FROM users WHERE inactive=true keeps other users; TRUNCATE users empties users; DROP TABLE users removes the table itself.
Previous Next
Q248 What is a stored procedure compared with a function?
ANSWER
Both store reusable database logic. A function normally returns a value and can often be used inside queries, while a procedure is called to perform a workflow and may manage transaction-oriented operations depending on the DBMS.
EXAMPLE
A calculate_tax function returns a number; a close_month procedure may update several accounting tables.
Previous Next
Q249 What is a database trigger?
ANSWER
A trigger automatically runs database logic when an event such as INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE occurs. It should be used carefully because its behavior is less visible to application code.
EXAMPLE
An AFTER UPDATE trigger writes the old and new account status to an audit table.
Previous Next
Q250 What is a correlated subquery?High frequency
ANSWER
A correlated subquery refers to the current row of its outer query, so it is logically evaluated for each outer row.
EXAMPLE
Selecting employees whose salary is above the average of their own department correlates the inner department_id with the outer employee row.
Previous Next
Q251 What is EXISTS compared with IN?High frequency
ANSWER
EXISTS checks whether a subquery returns at least one row and can stop at the first match. IN compares a value with a returned set; NOT IN needs care when null is present.
EXAMPLE
Use EXISTS to return customers that have at least one order. Prefer NOT EXISTS over NOT IN when the subquery may contain null.
Previous Next
Q252 What is a CTE?High frequency
ANSWER
A Common Table Expression is a named temporary query result used by the statement that follows. It improves readability and can support recursion.
EXAMPLE
WITH active_users AS (...) SELECT ... FROM active_users names an intermediate result instead of nesting the same logic deeply.
Previous Next
Q253 What is a window function?High frequency
ANSWER
A window function calculates across related rows without collapsing them into one row per group.
EXAMPLE
SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) keeps every order row while adding that customer's total beside it.
Previous Next
Q254 What is the difference between ROW_NUMBER, RANK, and DENSE_RANK?
ANSWER
ROW_NUMBER always assigns unique sequential numbers. RANK gives ties the same rank and leaves gaps. DENSE_RANK gives ties the same rank without gaps.
EXAMPLE
For scores 100, 100, 90: ROW_NUMBER is 1,2,3; RANK is 1,1,3; DENSE_RANK is 1,1,2.
Previous Next
Q255 Offset pagination vs keyset pagination?High frequency
ANSWER
Offset pagination skips a number of rows and is easy for page numbers, but large offsets can be slow and shift during writes. Keyset pagination continues after a stable ordered key.
EXAMPLE
OFFSET 100000 may scan or skip many rows. WHERE id > last_seen_id ORDER BY id LIMIT 20 can use the index directly.
